newsitem.title: TAIWAN: Taiwan stocks end at 7-yr high despite SFC move.
newsitem.headline: Taiwan stocks end at 7-yr high despite SFC move.

text.p: Taiwan stocks closed on Wednesday at a seven-year high, largely unrattled by the Securities and Futures Commission's launch of what it called a routine probe into credit trading practices in the stock market.
The commission denied the move aimed to cool down the red hot stock market.
The index surged to as high as 8,978.98 points and ended at 8,956.41, a gain of 38.24 points or 0.43 percent.
That surpassed a 8,948.49 close on May 8, 1990. The index has not closed higher since ending at 9,292.37 on April 30, 1990.
Turnover was heavy at T$166.5 billion, but much below an all-time high T$251 billion notched last Thursday.

"Investors interpreted the SFC move as aiming not to cool down the market, but to eliminate speculation, which is good for the market in the long run," said Taiwan International Securities assistant vice-president Alex Chiu.
Electronics, initially shaken by the SFC news with an early fall of 0.99 percent, rebounded to soar 3.08 percent. Chipmaker Mosel rose the daily seven percent limit to T$70.5.
Chipmaker United Microelectronics surged T$4.5 to T$116 and computer giant Acer was limit up to T$101.

"Expecting electronics to report improving sales and profit performance in the third quarter, investors were heavily buying the sector despite its recent surge," said Golden Securities research chief Albert Lin.
The index opened higher to reflect Wall Street's strong overnight rebound, brokers said.
Brokers also attributed the rise in part to the central bank's apparent reluctance to to intervene to cool the red-hot market, which has surged more than 12 percent since late May.
"Investors were encouraged as the central bank did not tighten its monetary policy to chill the market," Chiu said.
